_about: Clause library for the CiO Claims Desk. Entries are written from the FIDIC Red Book 2017 General Conditions on file. Cross-form equivalents for other books are clause mappings; where a form's text is not on file the entry says so. Edit freely — build_dashboard.py embeds this file into app/claims.html.

forms.name: Red Book 2017 — Conditions of Contract for Construction
forms.note: Works designed by the Employer; measured contract. Employer's claims go through the same 20.2 procedure. Text of the General Conditions is on file.

forms.name: Red Book 1999 — Conditions of Contract for Construction
forms.note: Still governs many live contracts. 28-day notice; fully detailed claim within 42 days; Engineer responds within 42 days; only the Contractor is time-barred. Clause mapping only — text not on file.

forms.name: MDB Harmonised Edition 2010 (Pink Book)
forms.note: Red Book 1999 with the multilateral banks' particular conditions built in (World Bank, AfDB and others). Used on most donor-funded Ugandan works. Mapping only.

forms.name: MDB Harmonised Edition 2006
forms.note: Earlier harmonised edition, superseded by 2010 for new procurements but found on older contracts. Mapping only.

forms.name: Yellow Book 2017 — Plant and Design-Build
forms.note: Contractor designs; lump sum. Same claims machinery as Red 2017; errors in the Employer's Requirements replace late drawings as the information-risk clause. Mapping only.

forms.name: Yellow Book 1999 — Plant and Design-Build
forms.note: 1999 claims procedure; Contractor designs. Mapping only.

forms.name: Silver Book 2017 — EPC / Turnkey
forms.note: No Engineer — the Employer's Representative agrees or determines. Unforeseeable physical conditions and most site-data risk sit with the Contractor. Mapping only.

forms.name: Silver Book 1999 — EPC / Turnkey
forms.note: Employer administers directly; 4.12 unforeseeable conditions are Contractor risk. Mapping only.

forms.name: Gold Book 2008 — Design, Build and Operate
forms.note: Adds a 20-year Operation Service Period; EOT is Sub-Clause 9.3 within the design-build clauses. Mapping only — verify numbering against the form.

forms.name: Emerald Book 2019 — Underground Works
forms.note: 2017 machinery plus a Geotechnical Baseline Report: ground conditions outside the GBR are Employer risk and time is adjusted through the Schedule of Baselines rather than a general 4.12 claim. Only a scanned excerpt is on file.

forms.name: Green Book 2021 — Short Form of Contract
forms.note: Simplified form for small or repetitive works. Clause structure differs from the major books; confirm the time limits against the form itself. Mapping only.

causes.name: Variation instructed
causes.note: No 20.2 notice is needed for an EOT arising from a Variation (8.5(a)); the Variation is valued under 13.3.

causes.name: Late right of access to the Site
Unforeseeable physical conditions
causes.note: Cost only — no profit; the Engineer may offset conditions more favourable than foreseeable.

causes.name: Unforeseeable shortage from epidemic or government action
Delays caused by authorities
causes.note: Time only, and only if the delay was Unforeseeable and procedures were diligently followed.

causes.name: Employer's suspension
causes.note: Cost Plus Profit, unless the cause of suspension is the Contractor's.

causes.name: Measured quantity exceeds the Bill by more than 10%
causes.note: Time only; the Engineer may weigh lesser quantities elsewhere but not reduce the Time for Completion.

causes.name: Any other delay, impediment or prevention by the Employer
causes.note: Cost recovery depends on the underlying sub-clause or the general law.

causes.name: Exceptional Event
causes.note: Time for any listed event; Cost only for events (a) to (e) in 18.1 and, for (e), only within the Country.

causes.name: Change in Laws after the Base Date
causes.note: Cost adjustment through the Contract Price; EOT if delayed.

clauses.title: Delayed Drawings or Instructions
clauses.plain: If the Contractor needs a drawing or instruction from the Engineer and it arrives late, and the lateness delays or costs the Contractor, that is the Employer's risk.
clauses.duty: Give the Engineer a Notice that the drawing or instruction is needed, when it is needed by, and what the delay would do. If it still arrives late, claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: The Notice must be given in reasonable time ahead of the need; the 20.2 clock (28 days) starts when the Contractor becomes aware of the delay.
clauses.risk: Employer — Cost Plus Profit and EOT — unless the drawing was late because of something the Contractor did or failed to submit.

equiv.note: Same test and remedy; claim under 20.1.
Becomes 'Errors in the Employer's Requirements' — the Contractor designs.
No equivalent; the Contractor carries information risk.

clauses.title: Right of Access to the Site
clauses.plain: The Employer must give the Contractor access to and possession of the Site by the times in the Contract Data. Late access delays the whole job and is an Employer risk.
clauses.duty: Record the dates access was due and given; show the effect on the Programme; claim under 20.2 for EOT and Cost Plus Profit.
clauses.limits: 28-day Notice of Claim from awareness; 84-day fully detailed claim.
clauses.risk: Employer, save to the extent the delay was caused by the Contractor's own failure (for example a document not yet submitted).

clauses.title: Site Data and Items of Reference
clauses.plain: Before the Base Date the Employer must hand over all relevant site data it holds — topography, sub-surface, hydrology, climate, environment — and keep handing over data that arrives later. The Employer also specifies the survey reference points.
clauses.duty: Check what was supplied against what the Employer held; the Contractor is responsible for interpreting it (4.10) but not for data the Employer withheld.
clauses.limits: None fixed for the Employer; the Contractor's setting-out Notice under 4.7.2 runs 28 days from Commencement.
clauses.risk: The Employer answers for the accuracy of the items of reference; interpretation of the data is the Contractor's.

equiv.note: Site data sat in 4.10 in the 1999 forms.
Contractor deemed to have verified the data.

clauses.title: Agreement or Determination
clauses.plain: How the Engineer decides a claim or a matter: first consult both Parties and try to get them to agree; if that fails, make a fair determination. Each stage has 42 days. The Engineer acts neutrally here, not for the Employer.
clauses.duty: Take part in the consultation; give additional particulars promptly if asked; if you disagree with the determination, give a Notice of Dissatisfaction within 28 days, otherwise it becomes final and binding.
clauses.limits: 42 days to agree (from receipt of the fully detailed claim); 42 further days to determine; if the Engineer is silent, a claim is deemed rejected and a non-claim matter becomes a Dispute for the DAAB. NOD within 28 days. Clerical errors: 14 days to raise, 7 days to correct.
clauses.risk: Procedural. A missed NOD converts the determination into a final, binding obligation.

equiv.note: Consult, then determine 'fairly'; no double 42-day structure — the 42-day response is in 20.1.

clauses.title: Co-operation
clauses.plain: The Contractor must make room on Site for the Employer's people, other contractors and utilities. If the co-ordination demanded was Unforeseeable at tender, the Contractor can claim time and cost.
clauses.duty: Co-operate as instructed; record what was Unforeseeable and its effect; claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: 28-day Notice of Claim.
clauses.risk: Contractor for foreseeable co-ordination; Employer for the Unforeseeable part.

clauses.title: Setting Out
clauses.plain: The Contractor sets out the Works from the Employer's items of reference and must verify them first. An error in the reference points that an experienced contractor could not have found is Employer risk.
clauses.duty: Verify the reference items; give a Notice of any error within 28 days of Commencement (or as soon as practicable for items issued later); rectify and claim if the error was Unforeseeable.
clauses.limits: 28 days from Commencement for items on the Drawings; then 20.2.
clauses.risk: Split: the Contractor answers for positioning, the Employer for an Unforeseeable error in the references.

clauses.title: Unforeseeable Physical Conditions
clauses.plain: Natural or man-made conditions on Site — including sub-surface and hydrological conditions — that an experienced contractor could not reasonably have foreseen at the Base Date entitle the Contractor to time and Cost. Climatic conditions are excluded here (they sit in 8.5(c)).
clauses.duty: Give a Notice as soon as practicable describing the conditions and why they were Unforeseeable; keep working; allow the Engineer to inspect and investigate; comply with instructions; claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: Notice as soon as practicable, then the 20.2 clock (28 / 84 days).
clauses.risk: Employer for the Unforeseeable part, Cost without profit. The Engineer may set off conditions that were more favourable than foreseeable, but not below a net zero.

equiv.note: Replaced by the Geotechnical Baseline Report: conditions outside the GBR are Employer risk; time adjusts via the Schedule of Baselines.

clauses.title: Access Route
clauses.plain: The Contractor is taken to have satisfied itself about the access routes to Site at the Base Date and is responsible for their use and repair. The Employer does not guarantee them.
clauses.duty: Inspect routes at tender; obtain permits; keep evidence if a route becomes unusable for reasons outside the Contractor's control.
clauses.limits: None specific; any claim runs through 20.2.
clauses.risk: Contractor, unless a route is closed by something that is an Employer risk elsewhere in the Contract.

clauses.title: Archaeological and Geological Findings
clauses.plain: Fossils, antiquities and geological finds belong under the Employer's authority. Complying with the Engineer's instructions about them earns time and Cost.
clauses.duty: Protect the find; Notice to the Engineer as soon as practicable and before disturbing it; follow instructions; claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: Notice 'as soon as practicable'; then 20.2.
clauses.risk: Employer — EOT and Cost (no profit).

clauses.title: Testing by the Contractor
clauses.plain: The Contractor provides everything needed for the specified tests and gives the Engineer notice of when and where. If the Employer's side delays a test or varies it, the Contractor can claim.
clauses.duty: Notice of the time and place of tests in reasonable time; record any delay caused by the Employer's Personnel; claim under 20.2.
clauses.risk: Employer for delays it causes; Contractor for its own retests.

clauses.title: Programme
clauses.plain: Within 28 days of the Commencement Notice the Contractor submits a programme in the specified software, and revises it whenever it stops reflecting actual progress. If the Engineer does not object within 21 days it becomes the Programme the Employer's Personnel may rely on.
clauses.duty: Submit the initial programme within 28 days; keep it updated; respond within 14 days to an Engineer's Notice that it no longer reflects progress. This is the record the Protocol's Core Principle 1 is built on — every delay analysis later depends on it.
clauses.limits: 28 days to submit; Engineer's 21-day objection window; 14 days to revise after a Notice.
clauses.risk: Contractor's document, but the Employer relies on it; a stale programme weakens the Contractor's own delay case.

equiv.note: Less prescriptive: no software or 21-day deemed acceptance.

clauses.title: Advance Warning
clauses.plain: Each Party — and the Engineer — must warn the others in advance of any known or probable future event that could delay the Works, raise the price or affect performance.
clauses.duty: Advise the Engineer and the other Party as soon as a probable event is known. The Engineer may ask for a Variation proposal to avoid or reduce the effect.
clauses.limits: None fixed — 'in advance'.
clauses.risk: Shared; a failure to warn can be weighed against the claiming Party when the claim is assessed under 20.2.7.

clauses.title: Extension of Time for Completion
clauses.plain: The Contractor is entitled to more time if completion is or will be delayed by a Variation, a cause the Conditions list elsewhere, exceptionally adverse weather (Unforeseeable against the climatic data), Unforeseeable shortages caused by epidemic or government action, or any delay, impediment or prevention by the Employer. Quantities exceeding the Bill by more than 10% that delay completion also count.
clauses.duty: Claim under 20.2 (a Variation needs no Notice of Claim); show the effect on the critical path of the Programme; expect the Engineer to review earlier determinations — the total EOT can go up but not down.
clauses.limits: 28-day Notice of Claim and 84-day fully detailed claim under 20.2.
clauses.risk: Employer for the listed causes. Concurrency with Contractor delay is assessed as the Special Provisions say, otherwise 'as appropriate taking due regard of all relevant circumstances' — the Protocol's Core Principle 10 is the usual yardstick.

equiv.note: No 10%-quantities limb and no concurrency sentence.
Adds excavation and lining rate adjustment through the Schedule of Baselines.

clauses.title: Delays Caused by Authorities
clauses.plain: If a public authority or utility delays the Contractor despite the Contractor diligently following its procedures, and the delay was Unforeseeable, it counts as a cause of delay under 8.5(b).
clauses.duty: Show the procedures followed, the authority's delay, and why it was Unforeseeable; claim under 20.2.
clauses.risk: Employer for time only; no Cost under this Sub-Clause.

clauses.title: Rate of Progress
clauses.plain: If progress is too slow for a reason that is not an 8.5 cause, the Engineer can demand a revised programme with expedited methods — at the Contractor's cost, and the Employer may claim its extra supervision costs on top of Delay Damages.
clauses.duty: Submit the revised programme under 8.3; adopt the revised methods unless the Engineer says otherwise. If the slow progress is an 8.5 cause, say so — acceleration instructed to recover Employer delay is a Variation (13.3.1).
clauses.limits: Employer's cost claim goes through 20.2.
clauses.risk: Contractor, unless the slowness stems from an 8.5 cause.

clauses.title: Delay Damages
clauses.plain: Finish late and the Contractor pays the daily Delay Damages in the Contract Data, up to the stated maximum. They are the Employer's only remedy for late completion short of termination, fraud or wilful default.
clauses.duty: The Employer claims them under 20.2; the Contractor's answer is an EOT that moves the Time for Completion.
clauses.limits: Employer's claim is subject to 20.2 like any other.
clauses.risk: Contractor, capped.

clauses.title: Consequences of Employer's Suspension
clauses.plain: If the Engineer suspends the work under 8.9 and the Contractor is delayed or incurs Cost complying or resuming, the Contractor gets EOT and Cost Plus Profit — unless the suspension was the Contractor's fault.
clauses.duty: Protect and store the suspended work (8.9); record the suspension dates and costs; claim under 20.2. After 84 days of suspension, ask for permission to proceed (8.12).
clauses.limits: 20.2; 8.12 prolonged suspension after 84 days.
clauses.risk: Employer, save for making good the Contractor's own defective work or failure to protect.

clauses.title: Interference with Tests on Completion
clauses.plain: If the Employer's side stops the Contractor carrying out the Tests on Completion for more than 14 days, the Works are deemed taken over on the date the tests would have finished.
clauses.duty: Give a Notice describing the prevention; the Engineer must then issue the Taking-Over Certificate; carry out the tests when allowed and claim delay and Cost Plus Profit under 20.2.
clauses.limits: 14 days of prevention (continuous or cumulative).
clauses.risk: Employer.

clauses.title: Valuation of the Works
clauses.plain: Measured work is paid at the Bill rates. A new rate is appropriate where there is no suitable item, or where a quantity changes by more than 10% and the change moves the item's cost per unit by more than 1% and the item is more than 0.01% of the Accepted Contract Amount, or where a Variation makes the existing rate unsuitable.
clauses.duty: Track measured quantities against the Bill; raise new rates through the Engineer under 3.7.
clauses.limits: None specific; the agreement or determination runs under 3.7.
clauses.risk: Shared through the remeasurement mechanism.

equiv.note: Same tests; MDB adds a 25% Contract Price limb.

clauses.title: Right to Vary
clauses.plain: The Engineer may vary the Works at any time before the Taking-Over Certificate, by instruction or by asking for a proposal. The Contractor must comply unless it gives prompt Notice that the varied work is Unforeseeable, will hurt safety or performance, or is beyond its capacity.
clauses.duty: Comply, or give the Notice with reasons; keep the record of the instruction; get the Variation valued under 13.3.
clauses.limits: Prompt Notice of objection; a Variation-driven EOT needs no 20.2 Notice (8.5(a)).
clauses.risk: Employer pays for Variations; the Contractor carries the risk of executing them.

clauses.title: Adjustments for Changes in Laws
clauses.plain: A change in the Laws of the Country after the Base Date — including new taxes, official interpretations and permit requirements — adjusts the Contract Price, and gives time if it delays the Works.
clauses.duty: Notice to the Engineer as soon as practicable; claim under 20.2 for the Cost and any EOT.
clauses.risk: Employer for changes after the Base Date; the Contractor carries the pre-Base-Date law.

clauses.title: Adjustments for Changes in Cost
clauses.plain: Price fluctuation. If the Schedule of cost indexation is completed, the Contract Price rises and falls with the published indices — labour, materials, fuel — using the formula and weightings agreed at tender. If it is left blank, the Contractor carries all escalation. This is the clause the CiO price panel exists to serve.
clauses.duty: Agree the indices, base values and coefficients at tender; apply the formula in each Statement; keep the index source evidence.
clauses.limits: None; applies only where the Schedule is completed.
clauses.risk: Shared through the formula. Note the Protocol's Core Principle 21: tender allowances are of limited relevance to prolongation cost — escalation and prolongation are separate heads.

equiv.note: Same formula approach; MDB includes the formula in the Appendix.

clauses.title: Delayed Payment
clauses.plain: If the Employer pays late, financing charges run automatically — compounded monthly, at 3% above the central-bank discount rate of the currency of payment unless the Contract Data says otherwise — without a formal claim.
clauses.duty: Include the charges in the next Statement; no 20.2 Notice is required.
clauses.limits: Runs from the expiry of the 14.7 payment period.
clauses.risk: Employer.

clauses.title: Termination for Employer's Convenience
clauses.plain: The Employer may end the Contract at will on 28 days' Notice, but then cannot re-let the work itself or through others, and must pay the Contractor for loss of profit and other losses under 15.6 and 15.7.
clauses.duty: Cease work as instructed; submit the valuation under 15.6; remove Contractor's Equipment.
clauses.limits: Termination takes effect 28 days after the later of the Notice and the return of the Performance Security.
clauses.risk: Employer pays loss of profit — a 2017 change from 1999.

clauses.title: Suspension by Contractor
clauses.plain: If the Engineer fails to certify, the Employer fails to prove its financial arrangements, pays late, or ignores a binding determination or DAAB decision, the Contractor may suspend or slow down on 21 days' Notice — and claim time and Cost Plus Profit.
clauses.duty: Give the 21-day Notice stating it is under 16.1; resume when the default is cured; claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: 21 days' Notice; the underlying failure must be a material breach.
clauses.risk: Employer.

clauses.title: Liability for Care of the Works
clauses.plain: The Contractor cares for the Works until the Taking-Over Certificate, but is not liable for loss or damage from the listed Employer risks — easement interference, Employer's use, Employer-designed elements, Unforeseeable forces of nature, and the Exceptional Events.
clauses.duty: Notice the loss or damage promptly; rectify as instructed; claim under 20.2 for the listed events.
clauses.risk: Contractor, except for the listed events which are Employer risk (Cost Plus Profit under 17.2's second part).

clauses.title: Consequences of an Exceptional Event
clauses.plain: War, terrorism, riot, munitions, natural catastrophe and similar events beyond a Party's control excuse performance and give the Contractor time; for the events in 18.1(a) to (e) — and for (e) only inside the Country — Cost as well.
clauses.duty: Notice of the Exceptional Event within 14 days of awareness (18.2); minimise the delay (18.3); claim under 20.2.
clauses.limits: 14-day Notice of the event, then the 20.2 clock; optional termination after 84 days' continuous prevention (18.5).
clauses.risk: Time for all listed events; Cost only for the enumerated ones.

clauses.title: Claims
clauses.plain: Defines what a Claim is: the Employer's claim for money or a longer Defects Notification Period, the Contractor's claim for money or EOT, or either Party's claim for some other entitlement. The first two go through 20.2; the third goes to the Engineer under 3.7 by a simple Notice.
clauses.duty: Identify which limb the claim falls under before choosing the procedure.
clauses.limits: Limbs (a) and (b): the 20.2 time-bars. Limb (c): Notice as soon as practicable after the disagreement.
clauses.risk: Procedural.

equiv.note: Contractor's claims in 20.1, Employer's claims in 2.5 — different procedures and time-bars.

clauses.title: Claims for Payment and/or EOT
clauses.plain: The one procedure for any claim for money or time by either Party. Notice within 28 days of awareness, or lose the claim. Keep contemporary records. Fully detailed claim within 84 days, or the Notice lapses. Then the Engineer agrees or determines under 3.7.
clauses.duty: Notice of Claim within 28 days describing the event; keep and, if instructed, expand contemporary records; submit the fully detailed claim (description, contractual basis, records, particulars) within 84 days; monthly interim claims and a final claim within 28 days of the end of the effect if the event continues.
clauses.limits: 28 days (Notice) · 14 days (Engineer's objection to a late Notice — silence deems it valid) · 84 days (fully detailed claim, extendable by agreement) · 42 + 42 days (3.7) · 28 days (NOD).
clauses.risk: Time-bar on both Parties. A late Notice can be waived under 20.2.5 having regard to prejudice and the other Party's prior knowledge; a failure that prejudiced investigation reduces the entitlement (20.2.7).

equiv.note: 28-day Notice; fully detailed claim in 42 days; Engineer responds in 42 days; time-bar on the Contractor only (the Employer's claims are in 2.5, with no bar).
Shorter, simplified procedure — check the form.

clauses.title: Obtaining DAAB's Decision
clauses.plain: A Dispute goes first to the standing Dispute Avoidance/Adjudication Board, which must decide within 84 days. The decision binds immediately; if neither Party gives a Notice of Dissatisfaction within 28 days it becomes final.
clauses.duty: Refer the Dispute in writing with copies to the other Party and the Engineer; comply with the decision at once; give a NOD within 28 days if you disagree, then attempt amicable settlement (21.5) before arbitration.
clauses.limits: 84 days for the decision; 28 days for a NOD; 28 days of amicable settlement before arbitration.
clauses.risk: Procedural; a missed NOD makes the decision final and enforceable.

equiv.note: DAB, 84 days, 28-day NOD, 56 days amicable settlement.

methods.name: Impacted as-planned
needs: A selection of delay events to model
methods.summary: Insert the delay events into the baseline and recalculate. Simplest and cheapest, but ignores actual progress and changed logic. Sufficient only where the contract dictates it or the event sits right at the start of the works.

methods.name: Time impact analysis
needs: A selection of delay events to model
methods.summary: Insert each event into the programme as it stood at the time and measure the predicted movement of completion. The Protocol's recommended method for a contemporaneous EOT application (Core Principle 4). Usually does not capture the eventual actual delay.

methods.name: Time slice windows
needs: A reliable series of updated programmes (the slices)
methods.summary: Cut the project into windows, usually monthly; each slice programme reveals the contemporaneous critical path and the critical delay in that window; then search the records for what caused it.

methods.name: As-planned versus as-built windows
methods.summary: Compare planned and actual in windows without relying on software logic; identify the critical delay in each window by practical analysis, then attribute causes from the records. Suited where programme updates are poor but as-built records are good.

methods.name: Retrospective longest path
methods.summary: Trace the longest path through the as-built programme back from completion to find the actual critical path, then attribute delay along it to events. Purely retrospective; sensitive to the quality of the as-built.

methods.name: Collapsed as-built
needs: A selection of delay events to remove
methods.summary: Remove the Employer's delay events from a logic-linked as-built programme and see how much earlier the works would have finished. Needs as-built logic that is often inserted after the fact, which is its main weakness.
